title: Darb Zubaydah pilgrim road
summary: The Darb Zubaydah was the main Abbasid-era hajj road from Kufa in Iraq to Mecca, about 1,300 km long, named for Zubaydah bint Jafar, wife of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, who funded rest stops along it. Wells, pools, milestones and rest-houses served pilgrims, with 27 major stations identified. UNESCO's tentative-list text calls it the most important hajj route between 750 and 850 CE.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO tentative list: the most important hajj route during the Abbasid Caliphate, between 750 to 850 CE; the first Abbasid caliph began improvements in 751. ASOR places Zubaydah's own hajj, which prompted her building, in 792 CE. The id says 790.

beats.caption: The first Abbasid caliph begins improving the Iraq-Makkah road with new milestones, fire-signals and rest-houses; work continues under al-Mansur.
Zubaydah, having seen the hardships of pilgrims on the hajj in 792, devotes her resources to improving safety and comfort.
The road, with 27 major stations, becomes the most important hajj route of the Abbasid period.
